How Strong Earnings Will Impact MetLife Stock (MET)
sum: MetLife reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$20.522b and net income of US$2.397b, with diluted EPS from continuing operations at US$3.67.
The company also amended and restated a revolving credit agreement that allows borrowings and letters of credit up to US$4.0b, with potential expansion to US$5.5b for general corporate use.
This analysis considers how MetLife's stronger quarterly earnings shape the existing investment narrative and whether they reinforce or challenge it.

Scan how MetLife's latest earnings and fresh credit capacity compare with other insurers by reviewing a curated 31 resilient stocks with low risk scores designed to pair resilient balance sheets with steadier risk profiles.

To own MetLife, an investor has to believe the New Frontier plan, cost control and international segments can keep supporting earnings quality even as headline growth expectations stay moderate. The latest quarter’s higher revenue and net income help that case, but the short term focus still sits on whether fee based lines and spreads can hold up.

The biggest risk flagged in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St is pressure on MetLife Investment Management earnings and Retirement and Income Solutions spreads. The amended revolving credit capacity looks more like plumbing than a catalyst. It adds flexibility, but does not materially change near term earnings drivers or risks.

The amended and restated credit agreement out to 2031 is the announcement that ties closest to this story. It gives MetLife committed access to up to US$4.0b, with an option to increase that to US$5.5b if no default exists, and facilities can support general corporate uses rather than a single project.

items.t: MetLife stock: Mizuho raises price target to 117 US dollars
sum: В четверг, 12 ноября, Mizuho повысила целевую цену MetLife на 5 долларов США до 117 долларов США, сохранив при этом рейтинг «лучше рынка». По данным Markets Insider, аналитик обновил свои модели страхования жизни после публикации результатов страховой компании за третий квартал и звонка эксперта по вопросам инвалидности.

Целевое увеличение основано на ранее поставленной Mizuho цели в 112 долларов США и сохраняет позитивную позицию брокера. Markets Insider сообщил, что пересмотр последовал за последними изменениями в секторе страхования жизни, а не за изменением рейтинга компании.

Отчет MetLife за третий квартал от 4 ноября показал рекордную скорректированную прибыль на акцию без учета существенных статей и роста доходов во всех шести бизнес-сегментах. Компания также заявила, что продолжает выполнять свои целевые показатели по свободному денежному потоку и соотношению прямых расходов на весь год.

Обновленный целевой показатель обращает внимание на то, сможет ли широкий операционный рост продолжиться после сильного третьего квартала. Для инвесторов основными показателями остаются эффективность андеррайтинга, инвестиционный доход и возврат капитала посредством выкупа и дивидендов.
Акции MetLife торговались на бирже Lang & Schwarz по цене 92,35 евро в пятницу, 13 ноября 2026 г., в 17:00 по центральноевропейскому времени.
Рынки США остаются более широкими площадками для страховщиков и финансовых компаний. Текущие рыночные отчеты дают более широкий взгляд на рынок.

Michael Burry trims Caterpillar bearish bet after puts nearly quadruple
sum: Big short investor Michael Burry has reduced his bearish position in Caterpillar CAT by 75% after his put options on the heavy-equipment maker roughly quadrupled in value, according to a post on his Substack newsletter, Cassandra Unchained.
"My Caterpillar puts have roughly quadrupled, and today I took them down 75%," Burry wrote in a November 6 post.
He added that the market value of his remaining position was now roughly equal to the amount he initially invested when he opened the trade at the end of the second quarter.

Caterpillar CAT shares declined 10% last week, marking their steepest weekly drop in 18 months. The stock came under pressure amid concerns over its valuation, production constraints, and uncertainty surrounding AI-related spending.
Shares rebounded on Monday, November 9, rising 7.2% to close at $598.88, following a broader market rally.

Burry's move comes as he continues to maintain bearish positions in other areas of the market. In an earlier Substack post, he described consolidating much of his bearish exposure into put options on the Nasdaq 100 and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF SMH, while also retaining puts on individual companies including Oracle ORCL, Palantir PLTR, MetLife MET, and Caterpillar CAT.DisclaimerContent provided by Seeking Alpha is intended for information purposes only, and that Seeking Alpha does not offer any personalist investment advice and is not a licensed securities dealer, broker, US investment adviser or investment bank.

MetLife stock posts record adjusted EPS as legal exposure lingers
sum: MetLife reported its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 4, with record adjusted earnings per share and revenue growth across all six business segments. The company said adjusted earnings rose 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars, while adjusted earnings per share excluding notable items increased 22 percent to 2.85 US dollars.

The results were published in a MetLife Business Wire release for the quarter ended September 30. Premiums, fees and other revenues rose 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars, while adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers increased 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars.

Group Benefits adjusted earnings rose 15 percent to 523 million US dollars. Retirement and Income Solutions posted adjusted earnings of 413 million US dollars, down 6 percent on a reported basis, but earnings excluding notable items increased 12 percent to 478 million US dollars. Asia, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and MetLife Investment Management also reported higher adjusted earnings.

The release said the annual actuarial assumption review reduced adjusted earnings by 46 million US dollars. Excluding total notable items, adjusted earnings reached 1.826 billion US dollars, compared with 1.566 billion US dollars in the prior-year quarter.

Separately, the Ontario Superior Court of Justice approved a 213.5 million Canadian dollar settlement on October 27 related to certain life insurance policies originally sold by Metropolitan Life Insurance Company in Canada. The Advisor.ca report said the agreement covers about 70,000 current and former policyholders and includes compensation and limits on selected policy charges. Sun Life administers the policies and has said it would seek recovery from MetLife under an indemnity arrangement.
MetLife stock traded at 88.19 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:14 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

For investors, the quarter highlights earnings momentum from underwriting, investment income and volume growth, while the Canadian case keeps historical policy obligations on the agenda. The company also said it returned approximately 1 billion US dollars to shareholders through repurchases and common stock dividends.

sum: MetLife reported a strong third quarter on Wednesday, November 4, after the US market close, with record adjusted earnings per share excluding total notable items. The insurer's official third-quarter release said adjusted EPS reached 2.85 US dollars, the highest quarterly level in company history.

Net income rose 187 percent year over year to 2.4 billion US dollars, or 3.67 US dollars per share. Adjusted earnings increased 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars, supported by higher variable investment income, broad-based volume growth and favorable underwriting.

Premiums, fees and other revenues increased 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers rose 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars, with growth in all six business segments. The figures indicate that the quarter's operating expansion was not limited to one division.

Adjusted return on equity reached 19.6 percent excluding total notable items. MetLife also returned approximately 1 billion US dollars through share repurchases and common stock dividends, while holding-company cash and liquid assets totaled 3.4 billion US dollars at quarter-end.

MetLife said it remains on track to deliver its full-year free cash flow ratio and direct expense ratio targets. Chief Executive Michel Khalaf described the quarter as evidence of the New Frontier strategy's execution and said management remains confident that it can produce repeatable results.

sum: MetLife announced its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 4, after the US market close. In its official release, the insurer reported record quarterly adjusted earnings per share of 2.85 US dollars excluding total notable items.

Net income increased 187 percent year over year to 2.4 billion US dollars, or 3.67 US dollars per share. Adjusted earnings rose 12 percent to 1.8 billion US dollars. MetLife said higher variable investment income, broad-based volume growth and favorable underwriting supported the result.

Premiums, fees and other revenues increased 12 percent to 14.1 billion US dollars. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding pension risk transfers rose 8 percent to 13.5 billion US dollars, with growth in all six business segments. The figures point to a broad-based expansion rather than a result driven by a single division.

Total return on equity was 42.7 percent, while adjusted return on equity stood at 19.2 percent. Excluding total notable items, adjusted return on equity reached 19.6 percent. MetLife also reported adjusted book value per share of 59.41 US dollars, up 5 percent, while reported book value per share fell 22 percent to 30.73 US dollars.

Chief Executive Michel Khalaf said the quarter demonstrated the strength of MetLife's New Frontier strategy and the discipline of its execution. He pointed to revenue growth in every business segment, solid underwriting, volume growth and higher investment returns. Management also said it remained confident that the strategy can deliver repeatable results and confirmed progress toward its full-year free cash flow ratio and direct expense ratio targets.

MetLife returned approximately 1 billion US dollars to shareholders through share repurchases and common stock dividends. Holding-company cash and liquid assets stood at 3.4 billion US dollars at the end of the quarter, within the company's target range.

MetLife stock heads into earnings with 2.71 US dollar EPS consensus
sum: MetLife is heading into a closely watched earnings date after analysts raised their expectations for the insurer's third quarter. Yahoo Finance reported on October 24 that the company is expected to publish fiscal 2026 third-quarter results after the US market close on Wednesday, November 4.

Analysts tracked in the preview expect diluted earnings per share of 2.71 US dollars, up from 2.34 US dollars in the year-earlier quarter. The projected increase would extend a recent run of outperformance: MetLife exceeded consensus estimates in each of the four preceding quarters, according to the same report.

The upcoming release will give investors a new reading on the insurer's earnings power across life insurance, employee benefits, annuities, retirement solutions and investment management. Yahoo Finance described MetLife as a global financial services company operating in more than 40 markets, with exposure to the United States, Asia, Latin America, Europe and the Middle East.

For full-year 2026, analysts cited in the preview expect earnings per share of 9.94 US dollars, compared with 8.89 US dollars in fiscal 2025. The forecast for fiscal 2027 stands at 10.72 US dollars, implying that the market is looking for continued earnings growth beyond the next quarterly release.

The comparison with recent operating trends is important for investors. Over the five years covered by the report, net premiums earned increased at an annual rate of 2.7%, while earnings per share rose at an annual rate of 3.3%. The third-quarter figures will show whether current earnings momentum is keeping pace with those longer-term trends.

Capital returns provide another date for shareholders to monitor. MetLife's board declared a fourth-quarter 2026 cash dividend of 0.5925 US dollars per common share on October 6, according to the Yahoo Finance report. The dividend is scheduled to be paid on December 8 to shareholders of record on November 3.

The record date falls one day before the earnings release, placing the distribution schedule alongside the principal earnings catalyst. For the stock, the key issues after the report will be whether results exceed the 2.71 US dollar EPS hurdle and whether management's outlook supports the estimates for 2026 and 2027.

items.t: Raiders Stock Report: Risers & Fallers After Thrilling Win Over Jets
sum: The Las Vegas Raiders entered their Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets desperately needing a win. After four straight games against the league's top teams, the Jets were, on paper, the team Las Vegas needed to get back on track after a tough few weeks.

Week 8 was supposed to be a manageable game for a Raiders team that has one of the league's toughest schedules. Las Vegas' road slate against the Jets is sandwiched between games against multiple teams with Super Bowl aspirations.
Las Vegas' offense woke up just in time to pull out a thrilling victory against the Jets on Sunday. Their defense played a solid second half, holding New York to 10 second-half points.

Falling behind early and trying their hardest to come back in the second half is becoming the Raiders' identity. Below are the players who are rising and falling after the Raiders' Week 8 loss to the Jets, their fifth straight loss.

Despite many narratives, Las Vegas' offensive line entered Week 8 in the top 10-15 in several statistical categories. The unit excelled significantly more in pass-blocking than in run-blocking. On Sunday, the unit excelled in both, helping Las Vegas jump out to an early lead.

The unit has its deficiencies, but when it comes to giving the quarterback enough time to throw the ball or escape the pocket and make a play, Las Vegas' offensive line plays well. Las Vegas' ground game was its most efficient in weeks because the line played well overall on Sunday.

Nailor's numbers have not shown the true impact he has on the Raiders' offense. However, Nailor's absence noticeably strained the unit in Week 6. His return made a subtle but significant difference for Las Vegas' offense in Week 7, opening things up, despite his lack of stats.

President Trump to present World Cup trophy at final, FIFA boss Gianni Infantino confirms
sum: NEW JERSEY -- U.S. President Donald Trump will present the trophy to the winners of the World Cup final in New Jersey on July 19, FIFA president Gianni Infantino has confirmed.
In a break from recent FIFA protocol, the trophy will be jointly presented to the captain of the winning team by Trump and Infantino.
At Qatar 2022 and Russia 2018, the two previous World Cups staged under Infantino's leadership, the FIFA president presented the trophy.
"We will be together with the president [Trump] enjoying the final and handing the trophy to the winner, of course, together," Infantino told Fox & Friends. "We are together all the time."

The decision to co-present the trophy follows on from the controversy surrounding the presentation of the FIFA Club World Cup to Chelsea after their victory over Paris Saint-Germain in New Jersey last summer.
President Trump was allowed to present the trophy to Chelsea captain Reece James, but his failure to leave the stage led to him taking part in the team celebrations alongside bemused players.
Although recent World Cups have been handed to the victors by Infantino and his predecessor as FIFA president, Sepp Blatter, Heads of State have previously presented the World Cup trophy.

items.t: Is MetLife Stock Outperforming the S&P 500?
sum: When thinking of insurance giants, New York-based MetLife, Inc. (MET) naturally commands attention. Founded in 1868, the company has built a global footprint, serving millions of customers across more than 40 countries with life, dental, disability, and financial services. Its market capitalization stands at $52.1 billion.

Companies worth $10 billion or more are generally described as "large-cap stocks," and MetLife is firmly positioned in this category, with its market cap exceeding this threshold, signaling both scale and influence in the insurance and financial services industry. Its straightforward business model, consistent returns on equity, and diversified offerings have earned it a solid reputation.

Despite the strengths, MET's chart tells a mixed story. Shares of MetLife touched a 52-week high of $85.29 on May 22, but since then, shares have slipped 2.2%. Over the past three months, MET has climbed 13.8%, which is impressive – and when comparing that against the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which has rallied nearly 10.4% in the same period, MET stock has outperformed.

Take a wider view, however, and the comparison becomes less favorable. Over the past 52 weeks, shares of MetLife has returned 5.9%, well below the S&P 500's 27% rally. The gap is evident in 2026 as well, with MET up 5.7% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis versus the index's 10.8% advance.

Still, the technical picture has improved considerably. After spending much of the spring trading below its key moving averages, MetLife has regained its footing and is trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages since April. That shift suggests buyers have recently regained control, pointing to strengthening bullish momentum heading into the second half of the year.

items.t: Manulife reports strong 2Q2025 earnings, recording net income of $1.8 bn
sum: Manulife Financial Corporation delivered a solid second quarter in 2025, recording net income of $1.8 bn, a sharp $0.7 bn increase over the same period last year.

Growth in Asia, Canada, and Global Wealth and Asset Management (Global WAM) offset U.S. headwinds, with the company also unveiling a deal to acquire a majority stake in U.S.-based Comvest Credit Partners, a move that will add $14.7 bn in assets to its platform.
Core earnings came in at $1.7 bn, down 2 % from last year on a constant exchange rate basis, but excluding changes in expected credit loss provisions, earnings rose to $1.8 bn, up 2 %.

Earnings per share climbed to $0.98, an 88 % year-over-year jump, while core EPS edged up 2 % to $0.95. The core return on equity stood at 15 %, and the Life Insurance Capital Adequacy Test ratio remained strong at 136 %.

- Asia continued to lead performance with net income of US$600 mn, up 44 %, and core earnings rising 13 % to $520 mn, driven by higher sales in Hong Kong and across other Asian markets. Annualized premium equivalent sales in the region surged 31 %, while new business contractual service margin increased 34 % and new business value rose 28 %.

Jaxson Dart's Dad Shares Message Lane Kiffin Sent Him About Giants Coaching Rumors
sum: A Jaxson Dart - Lane Kiffin reunion on the sideline at MetLife Stadium sure would be something, but the chances of it happening seem to be exactly zero.

With the New York Giants sitting at 2-7 on the season, Brian Daboll is firmly back on the coaching hot seat, which has led to coaching rumors galore. Following the Giants' loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Boomer Esiason, the former NFL MVP and now New York sports radio host, tossed out the idea of the Giants gauging Kiffin's potential interest in reuniting with Dart at the professional level.
Jaxson Dart's father, Brandon, decided he'd go directly to the man himself and sent Kififn a text message about Esiason's idea about him potentially taking over the Giants.

"As we were texting on our Kiffin-Dart family text thread, because I think Boomer Esiason had said something in the media today that maybe they should throw out a potential coaching (offer) to Kiffin, and he just sent it over with a smirk and just said, ‘It’s too cold in New York for me.’ It’s just kind of funny," Brandon explained on the ‘Bleave in Ole Miss’ podcast.

"But we have our weekly interactions with him and his family, and Jaxson holds high regard. I think Kiffin is one of his most trusted allies, and I think he uses him for advice in a lot of different ways, so there’s constant communication between them, even today, and there’s a lot of that between our families," Brandon continued.

Dart spent three seasons in Oxford playing under Kiffin after transferring from USC to Ole Miss ahead of the 2022 college football season. He threw for over 10,600 yards in his 39 appearances under center for the Rebels, who posted an overall record of 29-10 during his stint in the SEC.
As for Kiffin's note about New York being too cold for him, he very well could have been serious.
